ur10_collision_meshes.npz.note: Universal Robots' own collision STL files, through the rendered description. It replaced convex hulls of the visual .obj meshes in Isaac's URDF IMPORTER ur10 asset, whose frames are the other family: measured 2026-09-16, that bundle's links sat 1.8 to 65.0 mm from where UR's own description puts them, the upper arm worst at 52.0 mm of centroid. The same asset is the one whose Lula spheres sit about 61 mm off its own geometry, which build_ur_config.py already refused.

ur10e_collision_meshes.npz.note: Universal Robots' own collision STL files, pinned to one upstream commit, placed through the URDF rendered from their own config. Re-baked from the Isaac articulation on 2026-09-16 (owner decision, B5 S6): 26 of the 30 links of the five Isaac baked arms already agreed to under a thousandth of a millimetre, and the four that did not were mesh origins Isaac's URDFs omit, which UR declares. ur10e wrist_3 moved 0.500 mm.

what: Where each committed collision bundle's geometry came from, and a hash of the arrays the guard loads. A bundle is the exact mesh guard's whole authority and the file itself says nothing about its source, so this is what lets one be rebuilt, compared with another reader's, or retired. arrays_sha256 is over the arrays in name order, never over the .npz, because a zip carries a timestamp and the same arrays written twice give two different files.
